absent: Behavior of shared 32 bit entry, dispatch and user mode work helpers beyond gating and delegation shown here.
Number ranges and handler contracts for 32 bit and 64 bit system calls.
Full register state layout beyond the named fields.
External classification logic and APIC interaction for legacy vector.
Fast 32 bit handler internals and meaning of its boolean result.
Shared time, random and cpu node helper implementations.
Image, descriptor and patch site layouts with field offsets and sizes.
ChaCha constants and counter block layout.
Enclave run structure offsets and reserved range bounds.
Debug mask bits, direct call rewriting and KASAN helper contracts.

findings.text: Legacy interrupt gate for 32 bit calls is usable only from user context with kernel origin treated as fatal and externally classified events treated as fatal after kernel instrumentation context is established. Number handling narrows the value found in ax down to 32 bits into orig_ax while ax is marked with an error, before shared entry logic runs. Interrupts are enabled before the user mode work check decides dispatch, and control always leaves through the shared user mode exit.

FRED variant for 32 bit calls establishes randomized kernel stack context and instrumentation context from user mode, then enforces the same narrowing of ax into orig_ax with error marking before shared entry logic. Dispatch remains gated by the user mode work check with interrupts enabled, and control always leaves through the shared user mode exit. This fragment shows no kernel origin check and no external classification.

Compatibility entry for 32 bit calls passes register state through shared entry helper and then through a randomized stack work check that may suppress dispatch. Wide values placed in orig_ax by tracing are narrowed by the width of the return path, matching number accessor behavior. Allowed dispatch runs under instrumentation and control always leaves through the shared user mode exit.

SYSENTER entry for 32 bit calls rebuilds sp from bp and assumes the interrupt flag in flags was set in user mode. It then delegates to the fast 32 bit handler and returns the boolean outcome from that handler to its caller.

Table named sys_call_table provides dispatch indexed by call number together with declaration forms for normal and non returning handlers that operate on register state, plus a case dispatch form that invokes the handler selected by number. The non returning spelling initially differs and later collapses to the common spelling, and the table itself is populated from a generated header.

User mapped time services act as narrow delegations to shared implementations, covering wall clock queries, second queries, clock queries and resolution queries, in both legacy 32 bit time layouts and 64 bit time layouts.

User mapped robust unlock support exists in two widths that differ in pop pointer size, one for 64 bit pops and one for 32 bit pops, each accepting lock with tid and pop and returning the updated owner identity.

Robust unlock attempts a hardware locked compare exchange of the lock against zero and branches to distinct success and end markers built from stringified labels. Success clears the pop location with a width appropriate store while failure preserves state for interpretation through the returned value. The sequence uses caller tied registers with fixed roles and declares memory effects.

User mapped processor query fills caller supplied cpu and node outputs through a segment helper and always reports success. User mapped random query forwards buffer with length plus flags and opaque state with opaque length to a shared implementation and propagates its signed result.

Exception table entry holds two relative values named insn and fixup that locate a faulting instruction and its redirect target. Both are interpreted against the process mapped base combined with the image table base, and table length is derived from byte length divided by entry size.

Fixup declines debug and breakpoint traps unconditionally and requires a mapped image. It linearly scans entries comparing current ip against each insn location, and on a match it redirects ip to the paired fixup location while recording trap number in di with error code in si and fault address in dx, then reports handled. Absence of a match reports unhandled.
Provides a header guard named __VDSO_EXTABLE_H and an assembler helper that emits a handled instruction and fixup pair for virtual dynamic shared object exception handling.

Enclave entry moves among validation failure, execution, normal exit, exception recording and optional user handling with possible re entry. Validation accepts only leaves from EENTER through ERESUME and requires the reserved area to be all zero, otherwise reporting invalid argument. Execution uses a single asynchronous exit pointer for both enter and resume. Normal exit records EEXIT while fault redirection records leaf with vector plus error code and address. User handling when present runs with aligned stack plus cleared direction and a load fence, receiving exception state and untrusted stack, non positive handler results return at once while positive results re enter with the requested leaf.

32 bit enablement default named VDSO_DEFAULT equals 0 in one build variant and equals 1 in another. 64 bit enablement named vdso64_enabled defaults to 1. Fake 32 bit build defines CONFIG_X86_32 and BUILD_VDSO32_64 with CONFIG_PGTABLE_LEVELS equal to 2 while CONFIG_PAGE_OFFSET plus CONFIG_ILLEGAL_POINTER_VALUE equal 0 and CONFIG_NR_CPUS equals 1. Clock usage storage is marked mostly read.

Boot option named vdso32_setup parses an unsigned integer into vdso32_enabled, and values above one trigger a warning with forced disable. A control table exposes the flag with read write permissions bounded between zero and one through an integer vector handler. Registration uses name vsyscall32 under abi on 64 bit and uses name vdso_enabled under vm otherwise, performed during early init.

32 bit linker version script places clock plus time plus cpu and robust unlock symbols under node LINUX_2.6 with conditional membership driven by compatibility time and robust unlock options, and places entry plus signal return symbols under node LINUX_2.5 while hiding all other symbols.

ChaCha block routine without stack processes caller supplied output with key plus counter and block count using vector state. Each 64 byte block expands constants and key material, runs ten iterations each covering two rounds of add with xor plus rotate and lane shuffle, adds starting state to form output, advances output and increments the counter. After all blocks it writes back the counter and clears sensitive vector state before returning.
Image setup requires clock mode count below 32 and requires image size to be a multiple of page size, then applies alternative patching across the alternative range described inside the image.

Patch application scans descriptors strictly from start toward end so overlapping later sites overwrite earlier results, with KASAN disabled for the whole walk and re enabled after. Every site flows through analysis to preparation to application.

Analysis coalesces consecutive descriptors that share one instruction address into a single site and retains the largest original length among them. It validates the feature index against combined capability and bug capacity and chooses a replacement based on presence of the feature named by cpuid as inverted by a NOT flag. Site length must fit the staging buffer.

Preparation copies original bytes when no replacement is chosen. When a replacement is chosen it copies replacement bytes, rewrites direct calls when flagged, fills any leftover length with single byte no operation bytes, and then repairs relocations for the new placement. Debug builds may log old with replacement and final bytes.

Relocation decodes the staged bytes and biases branch immediates plus address displacements that point inside the replacement extent by the distance between replacement and original locations. Long unconditional jumps may narrow to short form when the adjusted target fits the narrow signed range, with surplus bytes filled by breakpoint bytes. Decoding failure stops further adjustment.
Width adapter for relocation updates supports one byte plus two byte and four byte stores and treats any other width as fatal.
Instruction address helper computes the target as the storage address of instr_offset advanced by the stored offset value.

System entry paths keep instrumentation context established while dispatch runs with interrupts enabled. Robust unlock achieves atomicity through a hardware locked operation with memory effects and without kernel sleepable locking.

Fatal outcomes cover kernel origin legacy events, externally classified legacy events, unaligned image size, oversize sites, out of range feature indexes, unsupported relocation widths and undecodable staged bytes which end adjustment with a warning. Enclave misuse with out of range leaves or non zero reserved words fails with invalid argument and never enters the enclave.
Debug print and byte dump helpers produce output only when selected by bits in a global debug mask and otherwise have no effect.
